findings.classification: missing terminal-event validation on Responses streams
findings.trigger: Responses SSE/SDK iterator ends normally after delivering partial text or completed output/tool items but before response.completed/response.incomplete/response.failed.
findings.impact: Ordinary calls can return a default successful stop/tool-bearing result without a provider terminal event; replay state is withheld, but downstream can still treat the model result as usable. Existing retry guards prevent generic replay after externally streamed output.
findings.counterevidence: Auxiliary source-summary mode explicitly converts an incomplete capture to error; transcription StepFun SSE already rejects EOF without its final event.
findings.smallest_alternative: Require an explicit terminal event for ordinary Responses completion and classify clean EOF as a typed transport/stream failure, preserving no-replay-after-delivery semantics.

findings.classification: cancelled/expired Codex OAuth flow can publish a late credential
findings.trigger: Token exchange has started; WebUI flow is cancelled/expired/evicted; no later login/logout supersedes the durable intent generation; worker returns after cancellation.
findings.impact: The flow Future/UI can be failed while the worker still commits the credential under the still-current login generation.
findings.counterevidence: A later login/logout changes the generation and rejects the stale commit; tests cover normal/invalid/timeout paths but the reviewed ranges do not exercise this in-flight exchange race.
findings.smallest_alternative: Revoke/supersede the durable login intent when cancellation becomes authoritative, then require commit_login to match that generation; retain joined cleanup and late-result discard.

findings.classification: fallback route transition can replay the failed primary before reaching fallback
findings.trigger: Prepared route certifies available primary; primary returns a fallbackable error before deltas; fallback remains eligible; circuit threshold has not opened primary.
findings.impact: Fallback verification raises ProviderRouteChanged before the fallback request; Runner clears the route and reprepares, allowing the still-available primary to be requested again before fallback. Cost/latency/request count can duplicate; no tool-side-effect replay is claimed.
findings.counterevidence: The stale-route test intentionally proves rejection of a preconstructed mismatched quote; it does not cover the consumed-primary transition.
findings.smallest_alternative: Carry consumed-candidate/attempt identity through reprepare so the next certified route begins at the fallback, while retaining leaf budget verification and stale-route rejection.

findings.trigger: BedrockProvider is constructed with api_key and creates its real boto client rather than an injected test client.
findings.impact: Construction assigns AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK in os.environ and never restores/clears it, so later same-process ambient AWS/Bedrock construction can inherit the credential. No deployed cross-account incident is claimed.
findings.counterevidence: Reviewed Bedrock tests mostly inject a fake client and bypass _make_client.
findings.smallest_alternative: Prefer an explicit SDK credential boundary; if the SDK only supports ambient bearer discovery, document/enforce one-account-per-process or use a non-overlapping construction boundary rather than leaving mutable process-global credential state.

findings.classification: physical provider-call observability is collapsed inside provider methods
findings.trigger: One outer safe chat performs multiple upstream transports internally: Responses compaction compatibility retry, Codex native compaction plus main request, Responses→chat fallback, xAI auth/hosted-tool retry, etc.
findings.impact: LLMCallRecord is documented as one physical provider-call attempt, but one outer record can cover multiple transports; request counts/error/latency attribution can undercount. This is not a claim that all retry/fallback records are lost or that token billing totals are universally wrong.
findings.counterevidence: Outer retry attempts and FallbackProvider leaves do propagate the observer and are separately recorded.
findings.smallest_alternative: Either emit a physical-attempt record at the common transport boundary or redefine the existing record as logical-call semantics and add a separate physical transport ledger; avoid double-counting outer retries.

findings.classification: direct runtime model/window setters retain stale route-owned capabilities
findings.confidence: high mechanism; ordinary active-session reachability narrowed
findings.trigger: Direct default model or context-window setter changes runtime identity without selecting a preset; generation settings remain unchanged; later admit() refresh sees unchanged generation.
findings.impact: The stored ModelCapabilities snapshot from the old route/window can survive into later admissions; capability-governed preparation such as source-summary max-output allowance can be stale.
findings.counterevidence: MyTool blocks direct model/window writes during an active session and recommends model_preset; preset resolution builds a fresh snapshot. Public/default-control and embedding paths remain the conditional reachability.
findings.smallest_alternative: Re-resolve/clear route-owned capabilities whenever model or context-window identity changes, or retire unsupported direct setters after D4 caller review.

findings.classification: xAI competing login flows have last-writer credential ordering instead of login-generation ordering
findings.trigger: Two same-provider WebUI xAI login flows are registered; newer flow completes/persists first; older flow completes later.
findings.impact: Each flow has its own lock and shared token writes serialize only at file level, so the older credential can overwrite the newer credential. This can select the wrong account after competing legitimate sign-ins.
findings.counterevidence: Logout clears/cancels registered flows before unlinking and refresh is serialized; this finding does not claim same-process logout resurrection.
findings.smallest_alternative: Give xAI login publication the same monotonic intent/generation ownership used by generation-aware credential coordinators, or enforce one active same-provider login flow and revoke the prior publication authority.

additional_observations.note: Preview can construct a fallback provider and actual traversal constructs it again. This is a P01 simplification candidate; eager-client leakage was not established.

PortableFileLock acquires its process-local lock before mkdir/os.open; those pre-try failures could strand the local lock, but production caller reachability was not established in H03. Retain for D4/P01 rather than promote.
Responses conversion keeps the last system message. Current runner recovery guidance was moved to user-role notes; a broader SDK multi-system defect was not established.
Codex CLI image adapter has real process/snapshot/hash behavior, but activation/external compatibility obligations remain unresolved.
Bound provider conversation replay requires a complete binding, exact transport receipt and replayable settlement; do not weaken it while simplifying providers.

finding_count_convention: Seven promoted H03 findings. Structural/retirement candidates H03-O1–O4 and preserved strength H03-S1 are not included in finding totals.

final_discussion_questions.question: Should every provider stream require an explicit typed terminal event before model output/tool calls become successful, and how should already-delivered deltas affect retry versus final error?
What single credential-intent/cancellation contract should Codex, xAI and future OAuth providers share across UI eviction, expiry, competing logins, logout and process boundaries?
When a prepared primary route is consumed and fails, should reprepare resume at the next candidate rather than replaying the primary, and what identity proves that transition?
Is LLMCallRecord a logical model call or a physical upstream transport attempt? Which request/error/latency metrics are promised externally?
Are process-global provider credentials/configuration allowed by a one-account-per-process contract, or must provider instances own explicit credential state?
Are direct default model/context-window setters supported public compatibility, and if so which route-owned capability/policy snapshots must be recaptured atomically?
Which provider/fallback construction and dormant compatibility helpers can be cached, combined or retired after caller/lifetime evidence, without freezing live auth/revocation state?

qualifications: H03-F1 is terminal-classification failure, not generic retry-after-stream replay.
H03-F2 requires exchange already in flight and no later generation supersession.
H03-F3 claims redundant primary request/cost/latency, not duplicate tool side effects.
H03-F4 is process-global credential contamination risk; deployed cross-account incidence is unproven.
H03-F5 is request-count/observability integrity, not universal token-billing corruption.

H03-F7 is competing-login publication order; same-process logout resurrection is not claimed.
